source: What is happening to me?
My head's not pounding any more.
Hamlet. Again.
So it's repeating again.
Why am I still alive? I thought...
No. I know I died.
Yes. There's certainly something strange going on.
I must go.
If things always begin like this, I'm going to be seeing quite a lot of Hamlet, aren't I?
Back at the beginning again.
Here we go again...
I've come to dread the sight of my bed-canopy.
All right, Hamlet. Come on.
His death—I see it with my own eyes! And—
—the traitor is your own blood. Yes, yes.
What? How did you—?
Hamlet, leave me be. I have things to do.
What number is this? Two thousand? Three?
I suppose it doesn't really matter anymore.
Enter Hamlet, stage left.
Another round, then.
Maybe I'll just go back to sleep.
I hope Quince is as bored as I am.
Go away, Hamlet.
What? I--
I know there's no going back from what I did. I don't regret burning that book.
Every minute of these four days is like the brick of a cell wall. And I've memorized them all.
But it's worth it if Quince can never hurt anyone again.
It has has to be worth it.
Come on, Hamlet.
Go, Hamlet. You're distraught. You need time alone.
What a strange dream.
Is someone there?
Hamlet? Is everything all right?
His death—I've seen it with my own eyes! And the traitor is my own blood, and my mother... Oh, God, my mother...
Hamlet. Stop for a moment. What in the world are you talking about?
And why are you in my bedchamber?
I'm sorry. S-sorry.
He looked so peculiar. Something's wrong.
Ugh. My head feels strange.
That dream seemed so real.
Lord Fortinbras's invasion is frightening and powerful.
Unaffected by internal affairs, his march seems to signal the abrupt end of my timeline.
Even if I am still alive...
Then what is keeping me here? What traps me in these four days? Why must I languish in this hell?
It's not fair. None of this is right.
There has to be a way out. There has to be.
Whatever lies inside that cursed book must be the answer.
If I can only find it...
Perhaps doing the spirit's bidding and finding King Hamlet's notes is the way forward.
If whatever's in those notes can raise the dead, then they're certainly powerful.
Perhaps this mysterious spirit everyone's whispering about has an answer for me.
If I can only cause it to appear, that is.
Perhaps the answer lies not in the future, but in the past.
Maybe there's something in the castle that can lead me forward.
So Brit is the person who's been after my life and spying on Norway's behalf.
It almost seemed so obvious I couldn't imagine it being true. She's always disliked me.
And yet--
She seems... trapped. In her own way.
I have to tell others about her, of course. I can't very well just let her kill me.
But maybe-- maybe there's a way out of this, for both of us...
Brit would have died for me, back there.
I can't believe it.
Of course, right now, she doesn't remember any of that. Right now, she hates me.
Still, I can't let that other Brit's sacrifice be meaningless.
Now I know. Fortinbras is hiding out in Castle Town. I have all the proof I need to find him.
All that remains to be seen is whether the others will believe me.
Father and Claudius had me taken to an asylum, of all places.
They thought me insane. I suppose I cannot lay blame with them.
It would appear that telling people things they find extremely strange raises the likelihood of me being labeled insane.
Perhaps I should observe when this happens, and consider who might find the information I know useful rather than disclosing everything to everyone.
Don't think I missed Hamlet leaving your room just now, Ophelia.
Ophelia! Why are you skulking in your room?
(So much for skipping my father's lecture...)
Only last night, we discussed—
Y-you're... is this real?
I can assure you, young lady, it most certainly is.
(This is so strange.)
(Everything's happening all over again. I know I've done this before.)
(Time is somehow repeating itself. I'm being given a second chance.)
(And that means... Hamlet will murder Father again, just as it was in my dream.)
(Someone's after my life, too. There really is a spy in the castle. And that person wants me dead.)
(I can change it. I have to.)
No mumbling! Speak clearly! How many times have I told you—
I know. I'll be careful around Hamlet. I promise, Father, I promise.
Only last night—
Hamlet accosted me. But I drove him out. Everything's all right, Father.
I must share this with the King, unless you have some further explanation to offer.
Father. What's wrong?
Only last night, we discussed this. Why did I see Hamlet coming out of your chambers?
Did nothing I say stick with you? Were you deceiving me?
I can explain—
And he was half clothed, too. If only someone else had seen him dashing out like that... I shudder to think of it.
I'm going to have to speak to the King about this. I cannot hide this from him. Unless, I suppose, you can offer some explanation for this transgression!
I'm sorry, Father. I don't feel well. I had such an odd vision last night--
A vision?
No. Never mind it. It's passed now. I'll sleep better this evening, I think.
Be careful, love. That's all I ask. Carrying on like this--it terrifies me. I don't want you hurt.
(I'm somehow being given... another chance to survive. I could change my own fate.)
(I should tell someone about my impending demise. But whom can I trust?)
Right. Sorry!
Greetings, Voltemand. Am I to assume this is the latest on Fortinbras and his men?
Thank you.
So the Norwegian prince accepted the offer. If only we could take him at his word.
This is exciting, but troubling news all the same.
The Norwegian prince accepted our peace offer?
This should be wonderful news for Denmark. Still... something in me feels unsettled.
I think the time may be ripe to tell the court about our suspicions regarding a spy in our midst.
It's time to start spreading awareness so everyone can keep an eye out.
I'll do so this morning.
My lord. Are yeh well?
Of course I'm not well. How could I be? You were there! You saw everything!
Perhaps you ought to lie down a while.
Or 'ave a drink. Yeh know, I've a bottle of brandy from the year you were born!
Prolly turned to shit by now, though.
Leave me, Marcellus. Your kindness is wasted.
M'lord, will you not even come to this morning's court?
I don't think I can face him. Not after what I heard last night.
But if yeh don't come... won't he be displeased?
I knew yer father well. He always kept a strong face in times like these.
An' so should you.
Come, m'lord. I'll accompany you.
So be it.
Marcellus, I fear I'm truly going mad.
Not at all, my Prince. Not at all.
Try an' wipe what you saw from yer mind.
But it was real, wasn't it?
I don't think I can face my uncle.
I'll stay out here.
As you wish, m'lord.
Thank you for inviting us back to the castle, Your Majesty.
Yes, it's good to be back in Elsinore!
(God's wounds if I can remember which is which. They're Hamlet's little schoolfriends, never seen apart.)
I thought I sent for two of you.
You did, my lord, but at the moment my companion Guildenstern appears to be missing.
You did, my lord, but my companion Guildenstern is...
I come alone.
I call you here to help my and my wife's predicament: Hamlet's melancholy.
My nephew's wits have left him as of late, and he's become altogether too dour.
We've heard tell of it, my lord.
But cheer is what we specialize in!
Yes, cheer and a little whimsy.
Good lord, you're both insufferably bright.
I've a task for you. One which is richly rewarded.
Uncover the reason for Hamlet's madness, if you can. Report all of his movements back to me.
A spying mission!
We can certainly attend to that.
Oho! It's not spying, per se—we're just worried about him. That's all.
Well, it's all the same to us, my lord!
We'll report back anything we learn as soon as we learn it.
I see. You want me to spy on him.
I can certainly attend to that.
It's all the same to me, my lord.
I'll report back anything I learn as soon as I learn it.
My thanks for your swift attendance. Let us hear the report.
My King, I have new reason to dispute the belief that Fortinbras' intent in crossing Denmark is peaceful.
When we convene the small war council in private, we ought to discuss further.
But not here. Not now. Privacy is critical in this, my lord.
Very well. We shall convene later.
Indeed, the circumstances are troubling. We are pursuing it with all options available to us.
My lord, as to the issue of Fortinbras... he presents a duplicitous face to us.
If there is some cause for new alarm, I should be aware of it.
Later, of course. A public morning court is not an appropriate venue for such matters.
Very well. We shall convene.
Fortinbras has decided there is no need to continue the bad blood between our nations, my lord.
He wishes for safe passage to Poland. That requires him to cross our lands.
Hmmm. A harmless enough request, given his recent peace offer...
In the interest of repairing our friendship, I will allow him passage.
Right, my lord.
My King, there is another matter!
My King, I also have a grievance!
Sorry to, ah, to interrupt the flow of the 'war chamber', so to speak, but it's a pressing personal concern.
Speak your mind.
Hamlet is acting quite mad. He threatens Ophelia's safety, and her happiness, too.
Oh, my poor Hamlet...
I agree, he's been doing poorly as of late.
I thought I had identified the cause. I thought he was merely lovesick.
Ophelia's given me reason to doubt that belief. However, what remains true is this: He's a threat to my daughter's safety.
But I believe I have identified the cause.
Hamlet is lovesick. He's a man obsessed. And he's after my daughter.
Do you have any further information on what Hamlet experienced last night to cause this behavior, my lord?
Why would I? I haven't the faintest idea where Hamlet was yesterday. Or last night, for that matter.
I see. But you agree with me that he's a danger to himself and to others at the very least, certainly?
